title: Cancer is a shrinking of the Self after gap junction closure

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cancer is a shrinking of the Self after gap junction closure

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure close gap junctions, and the consequence is transformation to cancer, in which cells revert to unicellular-like selves, shrink their computational boundaries and treat the rest of the body as external environment.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Indeed this occurs in cancer, where oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure leads to a closure of GJs (Vine and Bertram, 2002; Leithe et al., 2006). The consequence of this is transformation to cancer, where cells revert to their ancient unicellular selves (Levin, 2021b)—shrinking their computational boundaries and treating the rest of the body as external environment.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Metazoan cells undergoing oncogenic transformation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Gap-junction expression and coupling during transformation are well represented in public molecular data. These data can test association and selected causal experiments, but not the universal causal wording or the Self interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether oncogene or carcinogen exposure reduces junctional coupling before transformation and whether coupling loss predicts or mediates malignant phenotypes after controlling proliferation, damage, and cell type.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Observational association cannot establish that closure causes transformation.

Cancer is heterogeneous and some tumors retain or exploit gap junctions.

Shrinking of a Self has no independent standard measure.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.58
analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.58
data existence: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public tumor and exposure expression archives can test whether connexin genes fall with transformation, which is the measurable core of the gap-junction clause. Functional closure is only in scattered dye-transfer papers. The reading that cancer is a reversion to unicellular selves with smaller computational boundaries is not distinguished by those expression patterns from loss of coupling plus proliferation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare connexin expression, and where available dye-coupling, between transformed and matched normal tissue, and between carcinogen-exposed and control cells; the physiological clause holds if coupling falls as transformation proceeds.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Transcript abundance is not gap-junction closure or dye coupling.

A shrinking computational Self is not a separate variable from loss of coupling and altered growth.

Connexin loss is common in tumors and is neither necessary nor sufficient for transformation.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.65

operationalizability: 0.45
